section_summary: Pages 226–303 continue a statistical annex on Japan’s economy and standard of living, with historical tables and diagrams on production, income, consumption, population, trade, and war damage, followed by projections for 1953. A Tokyo despatch dated May 27, 1949 forwards two Japanese Foreign Office studies and discusses their choice of a 1930–34 baseline and estimates of the growth and trade needed for Japan to be self-supporting.

people.name: E. G. Seidensticker Jr.
people.role: Named in the despatch’s drafting initials

subfiles.title: Statistical tables and diagrams on Japan’s standard of living and 1953 projections
subfiles.about: Historical economic and consumption statistics provide a baseline for estimates of Japan’s 1953 needs, production, and foreign trade.
subfiles.summary: The annex continues with tables and diagrams covering output, national income, military spending, household consumption, food intake, textiles, raw materials, trade, and population. It estimates food, fiber, and industrial imports needed in 1953 and exports needed to pay for them. Its final tables compare manufacturing output across the 1930s, project 1953 production, and quantify wartime damage to national wealth and industrial capacity.

subfiles.title: Prewar Living Studies Prepared by the Japanese Foreign Office Concerning the Japanese Standard of Living
subfiles.about: Forwards 1947 and 1948 Japanese Foreign Office studies and evaluates their assumptions about Japan’s standard of living and economic self-sufficiency.
subfiles.summary: The despatch forwards copies of two studies and questions the 1948 study’s argument that 1930–34 was an unrepresentative baseline. It summarizes projections requiring higher national income, industrial output, exports, and shipping by 1953 to sustain that standard of living.
